name: Pink Lace
lede: Pink Lace is a very pale, slightly purplish [[pink]], named for the look of pale lace rather than any dated plate or survey in our sources.

sections.title: A textile image, undocumented coining
sections.body:
Our color library carries this name only through a plain wiki-sourced list entry, filed under fashion and textiles, with no dated plate, dictionary or survey behind it [1]. The pairing evokes the pale, faintly tinted look of lace fabric rather than any specific maker or standard [1]. Who first used this exact name is undocumented in our sources [1].

The nearest named color by measured distance is [[mimi-pink]], redder [2]. [[mauvette]], [[rosolane-pink]], [[orchid-pink]] and [[queen-pink]] sit further out, all darker and redder or purpler; [[pale-pink]] is the most distant of this group [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a match for this pale pink in only 2 of them, about 0.01 percent, rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [3]. A swatch this pale and this close to white is scarce across the whole archive, so a count this small fits the pattern for its family [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished canvases read as screen colors, not pigment identifications [3].
